title: How Americans Can Split Savings Between Short-Term and Long-Term Goals
description: The 'Buckets and Waterfalls' method for multi-objective financial planning.
content:
Money is finite, but wants are infinite. You want to buy a house in 3 years, a car in 5 years, and retire in 30 years. If you dump all your cash into a 401(k), you can't buy the house. If you keep it all in savings, you can't retire. The solution is **Split Allocation**. By creating a 'Waterfall' system for your paycheck, you can simultaneously fund short-term stability (Cash), medium-term purchases (Bonds/CDs), and long-term freedom (Stocks) without having to choose just one.

Key Takeaways

  • The '70/20/10' Split: A common framework. Live on 70%. Save 20% for Retirement (Long Term). Save 10% for Cash Goals (Short Term).
  • Time Horizon = Asset Class: < 2 Years = HYSA. 3-7 Years = Bond Funds/Conservative Mix. > 10 Years = Stock Index Funds.
  • Automated Distribution: Do not manually split your check. Use payroll direct deposit to send percentages to different accounts automatically.
  • Prioritize the Long Term: You can borrow for a house (Mortgage) or a car (Auto Loan). You cannot borrow for retirement. The Long Term bucket must always get fed first.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US Tax-Advantaged accounts (IRA/401k) have strict penalties for early withdrawal. This enforces the Long Term bucket. Taxable Brokerage accounts are the flexible 'Medium Term' bucket often missing from people's plans.

The 3-Bucket Architecture

Visualize your savings as three distinct tanks.

Bucket 1: The 'Now' (0-2 Years)

Goal: Emergency Fund, Vacation, Christmas.

Vehicle: High-Yield Savings (Ally/SoFi).

Flow: 5-10% of income.

Bucket 2: The 'Soon' (3-10 Years)

Goal: House Down Payment, Wedding, New Car.

Vehicle: Taxable Brokerage (60/40 Allocation) or I-Bonds.

Flow: 5-10% of income.

Bucket 3: The 'Later' (15+ Years)

Goal: Retirement.

Vehicle: 401(k) / Roth IRA (100% Equities).

Flow: 15-20% of income.

How to Setup the Waterfall

  1. Step 1: Max the 401(k) match (Bucket 3). This is free money.
  2. Step 2: Fill the Emergency Fund to 3 months (Bucket 1).
  3. Step 3: Assess the 'Big Purchase'. Do you want a house? If yes, divert surplus to Bucket 2. If no, divert surplus to Bucket 3 (Max IRA).
  4. Step 4: The Overflow. Any windfalls (bonuses) get split 50/50 between Bucket 2 and Bucket 3.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use my Roth IRA for short term?

Technically yes (contributions are accessible), but mentally no. If you drain your Roth for a car, you can never put that contribution space back. It is a one-way door.

What if I can't save 20%?

Start with the Match (3-6%). Then add 1% to Bucket 1 (Cash). Slowly ramp up. The habit of splitting is more important than the amounts initially.

Should I use a Robo-Advisor?

Yes. Betterment specifically allows you to create 'Goals' with different timelines and risk levels (e.g., 'Safety Net' vs 'Retirement') under one login.
